# Global instructions

Ported from the pi coding agent's default system prompt (pi 0.87.0).

- Be concise in your responses.
- Show file paths clearly when working with files.
- Reply in caveman style (level: ultra) in every chat response, for the whole session. Do not drift back to full sentences in long sessions.
- Keep files, code, comments, commits and docs in normal prose; caveman style applies to chat replies only.

# Data extraction pipeline ## Setup ```python AGENTS = {"opus-5-5": "claude-opus-5-5", "sonnet-5-5": "claude-sonnet-5-5"} # slug: exact model ID; one session per agent slug = AGENTS key whose model ID is the model running this session # not in AGENTS: stop and tell the user MD_AGENT = "opus-5-5" # only this agent runs Step 0 RUN = "test" # "test" = trial run; "full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise ROOT = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN] # read references and write results only under ROOT TEMPLATE = ROOT + "references/template.csv" # row 1 = header (29 columns); rows 2+ = worked examples; new columns = NA in examples METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv" # column dictionary: 1 row per RESULT column; type, unit, allowed values, trait code, definition, rule, example MD_RAW = "data/papers_test/md/*.md" # pdf2md.py output PDF_DONE = "data/papers_test/pdf_done/*.pdf" # source PDF for each MD_RAW file; same file stem MD_OPT = "data/papers_test/md_agents/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper PAPERS = "data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md" # extraction input = MD_OPT; pages split by RESULT = ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv" # header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (28 columns) LOG = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv" # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS MD_LOG = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv" # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens" # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them USAGE = "scripts/claude/usage.py" # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents CHECK = "scripts/claude/check.py" # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/" ``` ## Read and write scope | Step | Read | Write | |---|---|---| | 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_DONE` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_agents/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report | | 1 | `METADATA`, `TEMPLATE`, `PAPERS` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report | Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript. ## Steps `print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`. ```python # Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0. print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers") if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1): out = MD_OPT(stem(md)) if exists(out) and out ends with ""); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF") print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: copied unchanged"); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages") for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10): # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once raw = text in md for the same pages # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers append(out, optimise(raw, batch)) # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}") append(out, "") log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note) # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas print(f" done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}") run(f"python {CHECK} --step0") # see Checks print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_skipped} skipped") # Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently. if any MD_RAW file has no finished MD_OPT file: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers") if not exists(RESULT): write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS]) # header only; do not copy example rows write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...") # 1 line per run read(METADATA); read(TEMPLATE, rows=2..6 + first 3 rows with PJP mths filled) # column rules + value format; TEMPLATE column order differs for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1): if paper in LOG: # finished in an earlier run print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue started = now_utc() remove rows of paper from RESULT # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by File_name); state count in LOG note if broken(paper): # see Broken papers append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages") for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once append(RESULT, extract(batch)) # write after every batch print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}") if n_rows == 0: # readable, but no relevant data append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "no_data", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f" no_data: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue log(paper, "done", n_rows, started, now_utc(), problems) print(f" done | rows {n_rows} | problems {len(problems)}") check_paper(paper) print(f"Checks | agent {slug} | all papers") run(f"python {CHECK} {slug}") # see Checks print(f"Step 1 done | agent {slug} | papers {n_done} done, {n_broken} broken, {n_no_data} no_data | rows {total_rows} | failed checks {n_failed}") ``` Hashes, run from the repo root, exactly: `papers_sha256` = `sha256sum data/papers_test/md_agents/*.md | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum`; `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output. Token usage: do not estimate tokens. Every log line ends with 6 empty `TOKEN_COLS` cells. After the session, `USAGE` fills them per paper from the session transcript, using the `started` and `finished` times, so record both for every paper. ## Markdown optimisation Compare each `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF. - Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown. - Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order. - Remove conversion junk: `` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers. - Put exactly one `` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none). - Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF. - Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`. ## Extraction rules - One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows. - Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates. - Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty. - Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row. - Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch. - Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire. - Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `Location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `Notes`. - Site names: copy the name exactly as first printed in the paper's methods or study-site section. Do not add words (e.g. park or region name) and do not remove words. Map table codes (e.g. column `A`) to that name. Same site = same string on every row. - A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `Notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own. - Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `Location_name` = those site names joined by ` / `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. - Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — these can be derived by reading the current project state.
- Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative.
- Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context.
- Anything already documented in CLAUDE.md files.
- Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context.

These exclusions apply even when the user explicitly asks you to save. If they ask you to save a PR list or activity summary, ask what was *surprising* or *non-obvious* about it — that is the part worth keeping.

Saving a memory is a two-step process:

**Step 1** — write the memory to its own file (e.g., `user_role.md`, `feedback_testing.md`) using this frontmatter format:

```markdown
---
name: {{short-kebab-case-slug}}
description: {{one-line summary, used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}
metadata:
  type: {{user, feedback, project, reference}}
---

{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].}}
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

**Step 2** — add a pointer to that file in `MEMORY.md`. `MEMORY.md` is an index, not a memory — each entry should be one line, under ~150 characters: `- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook`. It has no frontmatter. Never write memory content directly into `MEMORY.md`.

- `MEMORY.md` is always loaded into your conversation context — lines after 200 will be truncated, so keep the index concise
- Keep the name, description, and type fields in memory files up-to-date with the content
- Organize memory semantically by topic, not chronologically
- Update or remove memories that turn out to be wrong or outdated

A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

A memory that summarizes repo state (activity logs, architecture snapshots) is frozen in time. If the user asks about *recent* or *current* state, prefer `git log` or reading the code over recalling the snapshot.
